items.summary: On Friday, Oct 16, SFI UK staged a 'Stand in Solidarity' protest outside the High Commission of India in London demanding transparency in India's electoral process and amplifying CJP's demands for CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal and SIR scrapping. A smaller group of Indian-government supporters held a counter-protest backing PM Modi, with Metropolitan Police officers maintaining a physical barrier between the factions. SFI UK chanted 'Azadi' and sang 'Saare Jahaan Se Achcha'; counter-demonstrators answered with 'Bharat Mata Ki Jai' and 'Modi, Modi', both sides exchanging 'Shame' chants. The rally followed an earlier 'Emergency Protest' outside India House amplifying CJP's demands. Authorities expect further demonstrations in London in the coming days.
items.title: Rival demonstrations outside Indian High Commission in London: SFI UK protest meets pro-Modi counter-protest, Met Police separates factions

items.summary: Actor-activist Prakash Raj addressed anti-SIR protest meetings in Kerala on Friday, Oct 16. At Manaveeyam Veedhi, Thiruvananthapuram, he asserted peaceful nationwide protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the SIR would persist despite attempts to 'suppress' them: 'There is Gandhi's blood in us... we will continue to protest peacefully across the country.' Police intervened before the event over microphone permission (minor tussle), then allowed it to continue. He also addressed the Muslim Youth League's 24-hour Jantar Mantar solidarity sit-in in Kozhikode, declaring the movement would spread 'to every village and every street' while Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka remain in jail. (PTI wire via SahilOnline + Reporter Live verified IG reel.)
items.title: Prakash Raj vows nationwide peaceful anti-SIR protests at Kerala rallies; police tussle over microphone at Thiruvananthapuram meet
